rv.q: Henry Shields leads the way as penguin-suited MC Sophisticato, whose magician father was crushed to death under 2.5 tons of props. Then there’s Henry Lewis as a hokey mentalist calling himself Mind Mangler, who tries (and, of course, fails) to read the audience’s thoughts.

Firstly, because they’ve teamed up with America’s leading magic duo Penn and Teller, remaining off-stage but guaranteeing that the illusions set before us – even the most deliberately-dismayingly maladroit – are top-tier.

A David Blaine-style stunt magician keeps pushing the limits of stage danger, getting more and more hurt in the process. A dancing pair of German magicians mix the elegant with the artfully clumsy. And the body count starts rising even as this “Disasters in Magic Charity Fundraiser” struggles to raise a penny.

There is also an overdone yet likeable central performance from Henry Lewis as a blustering mind-reader, the so-called Mind Mangler, who ends up mangling only his own career prospects. Lewis has been one of the clever instigators of Mischief Theatre and its string of Goes Wrong shows.

But the evening remains entertaining, and under Adam Meggido’s direction the performers’ comic and slapstick skills are on fine display. Lewis’s repeated botched exits are droll, Henry Shields channels John Cleese to fine effect as the evening’s MC – and there’s real magic to enjoy alongside the tomfoolery.
That said, if it’s not a work of genius, then Mischief are fundamentally operating within their comfort zone, unlike their misguided recent stab at dramedy, ‘Groan Ups’.

There's a mystical method in the madness. The highs really are quite high – Henry Lewis is a luminous presence as the wise-cracking Mind Mangler, relying on some whip-sharp improvisation to bring the house down when not stumbling through a ramshackle mind-reading routine.
